What else did we start? Storage, the Bus, payments and more

Storage-1, the Bus, payments on Base, Goose and our own DNS.

TraderSwift update2 min readRead Markdown ↗

Storage.

Storage became its own subnet chain, storage-1. Files stay outside the chain; the chain holds commitments and challenges, and storage providers prove they still hold a file by answering challenges from the chain.

On 18 November the launched test chain passed a full round: a real challenge, an accepted proof, and four refusals that left the state untouched. It is not a public network yet; the founding providers come next.

The TraderSwift Bus. The Bus is encrypted messaging between our machines.

Each message goes out under a policy, and the record of messages is anchored for audit. It speaks Nostr, so other Nostr tools can talk to it.

Orders never go over the Bus.

Payments on Base. People who build front ends on TraderSwift will be paid through x402, a standard for paying inside a web request, settled in USDC on Base.

The design is accepted; the wallet's payment side is in build.

Goose and Block. We studied Block's open-source work.

Goose is an open agent we plan to host unchanged before considering any fork.

The survey also points us at Buzz, Bitkey's recovery and Bluetooth experiments.

Our own DNS. A design for running our own DNS, with independent secondaries and a staged rollback.

It waits on the gate.
